q: A person has glucose 650 mg/dL, normal pH and negative urine ketones. What else is needed to assess for HHS?
c: Serum osmolality and the full clinical/laboratory pattern
A type 2 diabetes label only
Proof that nausea is absent
why: Hyperosmolarity is part of the HHS criteria. Glucose, pH and urine ketones alone are incomplete.

q: An adult with DKA has potassium 3.1 mmol/L. What is the key insulin safety step?
c: Start insulin immediately and assess potassium later
Replace potassium and delay insulin until potassium is above 3.5 mmol/L under protocol
Give a routine subcutaneous correction and discharge
why: Insulin lowers serum potassium. Low potassium must be addressed before starting insulin in this situation.

q: Glucose is 58 mg/dL. The person is awake and can swallow. What is the initial response?
c: Give long-acting insulin
Wait until the next meal
Give 15 g fast carbohydrate, then recheck in 15 minutes
why: The 15–15 approach treats a low in a person who can safely swallow. Repeat if glucose remains below 70 mg/dL.

q: A person with suspected severe hypoglycemia cannot safely swallow. What should be avoided?
c: Emergency help
Food or drink by mouth
Glucagon under the emergency plan
why: Oral intake creates an aspiration risk. Emergency treatment may use glucagon or IV glucose according to setting and protocol.

q: Which statement about insulin timing is safest?
c: Every NPH dose peaks at exactly eight hours
All rapid insulin must always be given 15 minutes before food
Timing varies; verify the exact formulation and plan
why: General onset/peak/duration ranges support planning, but product-specific instructions and glucose monitoring guide care.

q: A foot blister is painless in a person with neuropathy. What does that imply?
c: It still needs prompt attention
It is safe to ignore
A heating pad will speed healing
why: Reduced sensation can hide injury. Prompt assessment helps prevent worsening wounds.

q: Which food group belongs in the half-plate section?
c: Fruit and vegetables in any mixture
Nonstarchy vegetables
All carbohydrate foods
why: The plate method uses half nonstarchy vegetables, one quarter lean protein and one quarter carbohydrate foods.

q: A person with type 1 diabetes is ill and eating poorly. Which teaching point is correct?
c: Stop all insulin until eating normally
Wait two days before reporting persistent vomiting
Continue essential basal insulin with individualized sick-day guidance
why: Type 1 diabetes requires basal insulin. Illness needs monitoring, a specific medication plan and prompt escalation of warning signs.
